subject: general
question: The carbohydrates which are not used immediately are stored in the form of ________, which serves as the internal energy reserve to be used as and when required by the plant.
solution:
The correct answer is __**starch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants store carbohydrates in the form of starch, which is a **polysaccharide**.
 
• Starch consists of two types of molecules: **amylose (linear) and amylopectin (branched)**.
 
• It serves as an internal energy reserve for plants, used during periods of low photosynthetic activity.
 
• **Starch is stored in plastids**, such as chloroplasts and amyloplasts, within plant cells.
 
• When energy is required, starch is broken down into glucose by enzymatic processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cellulose**

 
 
• Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide and a major component of the plant cell wall.
 
• It is composed of linear chains of glucose molecules linked by** β-1,4-glycosidic bonds**.
 
• Unlike starch, cellulose cannot be digested by humans but can be broken down by some herbivores and microorganisms.
 
 
 
• **Glucose**
 
 
• **Glucose is a simple monosaccharide sugar** that serves as a primary energy source for cells.
 
• It is directly used in cellular respiration to produce ATP.
 
• Excess glucose can be converted into starch for storage in plants.
 
 
 
• **Glycogen**
 
 
• Glycogen is a storage form of glucose in animals and fungi, similar to starch in plants.
 
• It is highly branched and stored mainly in the liver and muscle tissues.
 
• Glycogen is broken down into glucose when energy is needed by the body.
